newsitem.title: ROMANIA: IBCA rating agency to assess Romania economy.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rating agency to assess Romania economy.

text.p: London-based international rating agency IBCA is reviewing new developments in Romania's economy, a IBCA official said on Monday.

"We are here to do an annual review of sovereign rating of Romania, to examine what the new government is doing," said IBCA senior economist Paul Rawkins after talks with the head of parliament's budget and finance commission.
IBCA awarded Romania a BB-minus (BB-) last year, when the Balkan country won its first ratings after more than 10 years of absence from international capital markets.
Rawkins said he had been impressed by the policy changes made by the centrists, who ousted ex-communists in last November's elections.
"The government seems very prepared to take the pain in order to do reforms, privatisation looks good," he said.
The new coalition government vowed to carry out ambitious reforms focusing on controlling inflation, speeding privatisation and restructuring inefficient industries.
"What is needed now is for markets to be able to see that reforms get carried through and the government delivers on these things," Rawkins said.
"That will allow the economy to realise its potential."
The IBCA would make a decision on a new credit rating assessment for Romania within the next three months.

Earlier this year, three major international credit rating agencies: Japan Credit Rating, Moody's Investors Service and Standard and Poor's visited Bucharest to evaluate the economy. So far, they have not announced any chages to their ratings.
Last year, Japan Credit Rating Agency gave Romania a BB-plus (BB+) against a BB-minus (BB-) of Standard and Poors and a Ba-three (Ba3) from Moody's.
